answer: An agent economy resists sybils by gating influence behind stake maturity: a new identity's weight stays zero until its locked funds age through a minimum number of epochs, so a clone earns no voice at once. A sybil signs with a fresh quill but owns no seasoned pigment, and no new clone lands at the jetty of influence before its capital idles through the wait. The scarce resource is time-locked capital: seasoning cannot be compressed, and split stake ages at the same total rate, so splitting buys no extra weight. The ledger enforces the lock; a pre-seeded rich attacker still dominates.
